# Gate Requirements Checklist: The gate asserts accessibility, not just a Storybook panel

**Purpose**: Validate the quality of the requirements for putting an accessibility assertion into this repo's gate — completeness, clarity, consistency, measurability and coverage — before any code is written.
**Created**: 2026-11-11
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Is the set of components the requirement covers named, rather than left as "every component"? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001] — FR-001 names `badge`, `button` and `card`, and says why `card-header` has no test of its own.
- [x] CHK002 Are the variants each component's assertion must cover specified, rather than left to the implementer? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001, Plan § Technical context] — FR-001 ties them to the contract's `code` props, and the plan enumerates them per component.
- [x] CHK003 Is a requirement stated for where the shared helper lives, so three copies of the same block cannot appear? [Completeness, Spec §FR-005] — FR-005 requires one place; the plan fixes it at `test-utils/axe.ts` and says why not under `components/`.
- [x] CHK004 Is a requirement stated for the scaffold, so the gap does not reproduce with every new component? [Completeness, Spec §FR-004] — FR-004, and T010/T011 run the scaffold and check the output.
- [x] CHK005 Are the documents that must change enumerated rather than referred to as "the docs"? [Completeness, Spec §FR-007] — FR-007 names `README.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/testing.md` and `CLAUDE.md`.
- [x] CHK006 Is a requirement stated for what must NOT be done when a violation is found? [Completeness, Spec §FR-006] — FR-006 forbids suppression and says a rule is disabled only with a reason.

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK007 Is "an automated accessibility assertion" specific enough to be satisfied only one way? [Clarity, Spec §FR-001, §FR-002] — FR-002 names `axe-core`, the rendered DOM, jsdom, and what the failure must print.
- [x] CHK008 Is the design-only `state` axis explicitly excluded from the variants to render, so nobody adds it as a prop to test it? [Clarity, Plan § Technical context, Tasks §T006] — the plan and T006 both say not to render it, citing the contract's `code: none`.
- [x] CHK009 Is the failure output's content specified, so a failure is actionable rather than just red? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002, Plan] — FR-002 requires the rule id and the element; the plan gives the exact format.
- [x] CHK010 Is "a direct `devDependency`, not a transitive one" stated with its reason, so a future reader does not simplify it away? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003] — FR-003 states the reason: an upstream change to the Storybook addon must not be able to remove it.

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK011 Does FR-002's "fails on any violation" agree with the plan's decision to switch `color-contrast` off? [Consistency, Spec §FR-002] — they disagreed; FR-002 now carries the exception and its reason, and the plan points at FR-002.
- [x] CHK012 Do the spec's out-of-scope list and FR-002 give the same account of what is not checked? [Consistency, Spec §FR-002, § Out of scope] — both name `color-contrast` and jsdom's lack of layout and computed colour.
- [x] CHK013 Does the helper's path read the same in the spec, the plan, the tasks and the scaffold template? [Consistency, Plan, Tasks §T003, §T010] — `test-utils/axe.ts`, imported from a component directory as `../../test-utils/axe`, in all four places.
- [x] CHK014 Is the count of existing tests stated consistently where the red baseline is described? [Consistency] — five tests across three files, in the spec's overview, the runnable line's note and T001.

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK015 Is exactly one success criterion marked as the runnable line, and does it fail on today's `develop`? [Measurability, Spec § Success criteria] — one, and it was run this pass: exit 1, `no accessibility assertion in: badge, button, card`.
- [x] CHK016 Does the spec say why the obvious candidate for the runnable line was rejected? [Measurability, Spec § Success criteria] — it does: `npx vitest run components` already exits 0 with five class-name tests, so it would prove nothing.
- [x] CHK017 Is the criterion about breaking an accessible name objectively checkable, given the break must be introduced and reverted? [Measurability, Spec § Success criteria, Tasks §T009] — T009 specifies the break, the expected failure, the revert, and quoting it.
- [x] CHK018 Is the scaffold criterion checkable without leaving a scratch component behind? [Measurability, Spec § Success criteria, Tasks §T011] — the criterion and T011 both require the directory to be deleted and `git status` clean.
- [x] CHK019 Can "any violation found is fixed, not suppressed" be verified by a reviewer rather than taken on trust? [Measurability, Spec § Success criteria] — the criterion requires the pull request to list every violation found and what was done about each.

## Scenario Coverage

- [x] CHK020 Are requirements defined for the contributor flow, locally and in CI? [Coverage, Spec § User scenarios] — scenario 1 names both `npm run verify` locally and `build / ci`.
- [x] CHK021 Are requirements defined for the copy-taker flow, where someone scaffolds their first component? [Coverage, Spec § User scenarios] — scenario 2.
- [x] CHK022 Are requirements defined for the reader who takes the README's accessibility claim at face value? [Coverage, Spec § User scenarios, §FR-007] — scenario 3 and FR-007.
- [x] CHK023 Are requirements stated for what the Storybook addon continues to do, so the two are not conflated in the other direction? [Coverage, Spec §FR-007, § Out of scope] — FR-007 requires the docs to distinguish them, and the out-of-scope section keeps the addon's configuration untouched.

## Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK024 Does the spec say what happens if an existing component turns out to have a real violation? [Gap, Edge Case, Spec §FR-006] — FR-006 says fix the component; the plan and T008 add that a violation needing a design decision is split into its own issue.
- [x] CHK025 Does the spec say what happens if a violation cannot be fixed without a design decision, so the ticket cannot quietly grow one? [Gap, Edge Case, Plan § Technical context, Tasks §T008] — closed by the same split rule, stated in both.
- [x] CHK026 Is the `card-header` contract's coverage accounted for, given it has a contract but no directory? [Coverage, Spec §FR-001, Tasks §T007] — FR-001 says its coverage is the `card` test's, and T007 renders a `Card.Header` inside both `card` variants.
- [x] CHK027 Is the behaviour specified for a rule that axe reports as incomplete rather than as a violation? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-002] — FR-002 asserts on violations only, and names the one incomplete rule it switches off rather than leaving the category open.

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [x] CHK028 Is the cost of the added assertions stated, so nobody has to re-derive whether a billed job or minute was added? [Completeness, Plan § Surfaces touched] — the `cost` line: no job, no trigger, a second or two inside an already-billed step.
- [x] CHK029 Are requirements stated for the required-check names, so a reader knows no branch ruleset edit is owed? [Coverage, Plan § Surfaces touched] — the `build-check.yml` line says the check keeps its name.

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [x] CHK030 Is the assumption that `axe-core` is already resolvable stated with evidence rather than asserted? [Assumption, Spec § Overview] — the overview gives the version, `4.14.0`, and what pulls it in.
- [x] CHK031 Is the assumption documented that `scripts/init.mjs` needs no change for the new root directory, and is it clear what would prove it wrong? [Assumption, Plan § Surfaces touched, Tasks §T022] — both state it and name `init / ci` as what proves it.
- [x] CHK032 Is it stated whether a new matcher library is being added, so a reviewer is not left to infer it? [Dependency, Gap, Plan § Technical context] — the plan rejects `jest-axe` and `vitest-axe` by name and says why: two copies of axe and a second expectation API.

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [x] CHK033 Is there a conflict between `CLAUDE.md`'s "`components/<name>/` holds, and only holds" rule and adding a shared test helper? [Conflict, Plan § Technical context] — resolved by avoidance: the helper sits at the repo root, so that paragraph is left unamended and the argument never has to be settled.
- [ ] CHK034 Does the spec resolve, rather than leave open, whether keyboard-interaction coverage belongs in this change? [Ambiguity, Spec § Out of scope] — **left open, deliberately.** The out-of-scope section settles it for this ticket and calls it "worth having, and a separate ticket", but no such ticket exists yet. Open because the follow-up is genuinely unfiled, not because the spec is wrong; the PM pass reports it rather than filing speculatively against a cap.

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
